Apple___Apple_scab.description: Fungal disease causing olive-green to dark brown scabby lesions on leaves and fruit.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Velvety spots on leaves, cracked scabby lesions on fruit, premature leaf drop.
Apple___Apple_scab.causes: Venturia inaequalis fungus spread by rain splash and humid spring weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Apply protectant fungicides at green tip through primary infection period; remove fallen leaves.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, prune for airflow, apply dormant copper sprays.
Apple___Apple_scab.pesticide: Myclobutanil or captan per label during primary scab season.
Apple___Apple_scab.organic_solution: Sulfur or lime-sulfur sprays; rigorous sanitation of leaf litter.

Apple___Black_rot.description: Fungal disease affecting fruit, leaves, and branches with rot and cankers.
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown leaf spots, frog-eye leaf lesions, shriveled mummified fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.causes: Botryosphaeria obtusa; overwintering in mummified fruit and wood.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Prune infected wood; fungicide sprays from pink bud through cover sprays.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Remove mummies and cankers; maintain tree vigor and balanced nutrition.
Apple___Black_rot.pesticide: Thiophanate-methyl or captan in cover spray program.
Apple___Black_rot.organic_solution: Remove infected debris; copper sprays at dormancy.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Rust disease requiring both apple and cedar/juniper hosts.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Yellow-orange leaf spots; cup-shaped structures on undersides; fruit lesions.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.causes: Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae; spores from nearby junipers in spring.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Fungicides at pink through early summer; remove nearby junipers if feasible.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Resistant cultivars; avoid planting near eastern red cedar.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.pesticide: Myclobutanil or triadimefon during spore release period.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.organic_solution: Sulfur sprays; increase distance from juniper hosts.

Apple___healthy.description: No disease detected; foliage and fruit appear healthy.
Apple___healthy.symptoms: Uniform green leaves, no scab, rot, or rust lesions.
Apple___healthy.causes: Good cultural practices and effective disease management.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Balanced nutrition, pruning, sanitation, and timely sprays when needed.
Apple___healthy.organic_solution: Maintain organic spray schedule only if history of disease pressure.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Fungal leaf spots reducing photosynthetic area in corn.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Rectangular gray-brown lesions between veins; may merge on lower leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.causes: Cercospora zeae-maydis; crop residue, warm humid weather.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: Foliar fungicides if economic threshold reached before tassel.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Crop rotation, tillage of residue, resistant hybrids.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.pesticide: Strobilurin or triazole fungicides per local extension guidelines.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.organic_solution: Rotation and residue management; limited organic fungicide options in field corn.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Rust pustules on corn leaves reducing yield in severe cases.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small cinnamon-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.causes: Puccinia sorghi; cool moist conditions favor development.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: Fungicide if detected before or at silking in susceptible hybrids.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.pesticide: Triazole or mixed-mode fungicides when threshold met.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.organic_solution: Resistant varieties; avoid late planting in high-pressure regions.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Large elliptical gray-green lesions on corn leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Cigar-shaped lesions 1–6 inches long; may cause top leaf death.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.causes: Exserohilum turcicum; infected residue, moderate temperatures, high humidity.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Fungicide application at VT–R1 if disease present and hybrid susceptible.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.organic_solution: Tillage and rotation; select resistant seed.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: Corn plants show no significant foliar disease.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Green leaves without characteristic lesion patterns.

Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease causing leaf and fruit spots on pepper.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots turning brown; leaf yellowing and defoliation.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.causes: Xanthomonas species; seedborne, splashing rain, warm humid weather.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Copper-based bactericides; remove severely infected plants.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified seed, avoid overhead irrigation, crop rotation.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.organic_solution: Copper sprays; hot-water treated seed; resistant varieties.

Pepper__bell___healthy.description: Pepper plants appear healthy with no bacterial spotting.
Pepper__bell___healthy.symptoms: Glossy green leaves and uniform fruit development.
Pepper__bell___healthy.causes: Good sanitation and dry foliage management.
Pepper__bell___healthy.prevention: Drip irrigation, mulch, avoid working wet plants.
Pepper__bell___healthy.organic_solution: Regular scouting; beneficial habitat for natural enemies.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Common fungal leaf blight on potato and tomato family crops.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark concentric rings (target spots), yellow halo, lower leaf loss.
Potato___Early_blight.causes: Alternaria solani; stressed plants, alternating warm wet periods.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Protectant and systemic fungicides on schedule after first symptoms.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Adequate nitrogen, mulch, rotation, remove volunteer potatoes.
Potato___Early_blight.organic_solution: Copper or Bacillus subtilis; strengthen plant nutrition.

Potato___Late_blight.description: Destructive oomycete disease that can destroy fields rapidly.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions, white sporulation on undersides, tuber rot.
Potato___Late_blight.causes: Phytophthora infestans; cool wet weather, infected seed or volunteers.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Immediate fungicide program; destroy cull piles; harvest timing critical.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Certified seed, hilling, forecast-based sprays, eliminate volunteers.
Potato___Late_blight.pesticide: Mandipropamid, fluopicolide, or cymoxanil + protectant per resistance management.
Potato___Late_blight.organic_solution: Copper hydroxide; strict sanitation; resistant varieties where available.

Potato___healthy.description: Potato foliage shows no blight or significant spotting.
Potato___healthy.symptoms: Healthy green canopy, normal tuber development.
Potato___healthy.causes: Proactive blight management and dry foliage periods.
Potato___healthy.treatment: Continue late blight monitoring in wet seasons.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Certified seed, good drainage, balanced fertility.
Potato___healthy.pesticide: Not required unless forecast shows high blight risk.
Potato___healthy.organic_solution: Preventive copper only when regional alerts active.

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease causing leaf and fruit lesions on tomato.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small greasy spots on leaves and fruit; defoliation in severe cases.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.causes: Xanthomonas spp.; splashing water, contaminated tools and seed.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.treatment: Copper sprays; remove infected transplants; avoid leaf wetness.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.prevention: Pathogen-free seed, greenhouse sanitation, drip irrigation.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.pesticide: Copper + mancozeb on 7–10 day intervals when wet.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.organic_solution: Copper bactericides; resistant cultivars; crop rotation.

Tomato_Early_blight.description: Alternaria leaf blight common in tomato production worldwide.
Tomato_Early_blight.symptoms: Target-like brown lesions, yellowing, defoliation from bottom up.
Tomato_Early_blight.causes: Alternaria solani; crop residue, plant stress, splashing irrigation.
Tomato_Early_blight.treatment: Chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin; remove lower infected leaves.
Tomato_Early_blight.prevention: Stake and prune, mulch, 3-year rotation, balanced nutrition.
Tomato_Early_blight.organic_solution: Copper, sulfur; compost tea support; resistant varieties.

Tomato_Late_blight.description: Fast-moving Phytophthora disease affecting tomato leaves and fruit.
Tomato_Late_blight.symptoms: Large irregular brown lesions, white mold in humidity, fruit rot.
Tomato_Late_blight.causes: Phytophthora infestans; cool nights and warm wet days.
Tomato_Late_blight.treatment: Aggressive fungicide program immediately; rogue infected plants.
Tomato_Late_blight.prevention: Monitor forecasts, use tolerant varieties, improve airflow.
Tomato_Late_blight.pesticide: Oxathiapiprolin or mandipropamid mixes per local guidelines.
Tomato_Late_blight.organic_solution: Copper sprays; destroy infected plants promptly.

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.description: Fungal disease favored by high humidity especially in greenhouses.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Yellow patches on upper leaf surface; olive mold on undersides.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.causes: Passalora fulva (Cladosporium fulvum); poor ventilation, high RH.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.treatment: Improve ventilation; fungicides on affected foliage.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.prevention: Dehumidify, resistant cultivars, avoid overhead watering indoors.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.pesticide: Chlorothalonil or difenoconazole in greenhouse programs.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.organic_solution: Reduce humidity; sulfur where temperature allows.

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Fungal leaf spot with many small circular lesions.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small circular spots with gray centers and dark borders; yellowing.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.causes: Septoria lycopersici; splashing rain, infected debris.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Protectant fungicides after first symptoms; remove lower leaves.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Mulch, stake plants, rotate away from solanaceae 2+ years.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.pesticide: Chlorothalonil or copper on 7–14 day schedule.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.organic_solution: Copper; remove infected lower leaves; crop rotation.

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.description: Arachnid pest causing stippling and bronzing of tomato leaves.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.symptoms: Fine stippling, webbing on undersides, leaf bronzing and drop.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.causes: Tetranychus urticae; hot dry conditions, dust, lack of predators.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.treatment: Miticides or horticultural oil; increase humidity slightly if possible.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.prevention: Avoid over-fertilization with nitrogen; release predatory mites in greenhouses.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.pesticide: Abamectin or spiromesifen per label; rotate modes of action.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.organic_solution: Insecticidal soap, neem oil, predatory Phytoseiulus mites.

Tomato__Target_Spot.description: Fungal leaf disease with concentric target-like lesions.
Tomato__Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown lesions with concentric rings on leaves and sometimes fruit.
Tomato__Target_Spot.causes: Corynespora cassiicola; warm humid conditions, crop debris.
Tomato__Target_Spot.treatment: Fungicides when disease appears early in canopy.
Tomato__Target_Spot.prevention: Rotation, debris removal, greenhouse humidity control.
Tomato__Target_Spot.organic_solution: Sanitation; copper where permitted; airflow improvement.

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.description: Virus disease transmitted by whiteflies causing severe stunting.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward leaf curl, yellowing, stunted growth, reduced fruit set.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.treatment: No cure—remove infected plants; control whitefly vectors.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.prevention: Reflective mulches, resistant varieties, insect-proof nets, vector control.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.pesticide: Imidacloprid or spirotetramat for whitefly per IPM guidelines.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.organic_solution: Yellow sticky traps, neem, reflective mulch, rogue infected plants.

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Viral disease causing mosaic patterns and distorted leaves.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green leaves, fern-leaf distortion, stunting.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.causes: Tomato mosaic virus; mechanical spread on hands and tools.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: No cure—remove infected plants; disinfect tools with 10% bleach.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: TMV-resistant varieties, hand washing, no smoking near plants.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.pesticide: Not applicable for virus; focus on prevention.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.organic_solution: Resistant seed; strict hygiene; destroy infected material.

Tomato_healthy.description: Tomato plants appear healthy with vigorous green foliage.
Tomato_healthy.symptoms: No characteristic disease lesions or virus symptoms.
Tomato_healthy.causes: Good IPM, hygiene, and environmental management.
Tomato_healthy.treatment: Continue regular scouting and preventive care.
Tomato_healthy.prevention: Mulch, stake, drip irrigate, rotate crops, use clean seed.
Tomato_healthy.organic_solution: Support beneficial insects; maintain balanced soil fertility.
